_sources.argenziano_1998: Argenziano G. et al., Epiluminescence microscopy for the diagnosis of doubtful melanocytic skin lesions: comparison of the ABCD rule of dermatoscopy and a new 7-point checklist based on pattern analysis. Arch Dermatol 134(12), 1998. Source of the seven criteria and their formal definitions.
_sources.argenziano_2011: Seven-point checklist of dermoscopy revisited. Br J Dermatol, 2011. Revised scoring where each criterion counts 1 point (total 7) rather than the original 2/2/2/1/1/1/1.
_sources.criterion_definitions: DermLite 7-point checklist course, https://dermlite.com/pages/7-point-checklist -- reproduces the Argenziano criterion definitions and histological correlates in full, freely accessible. Cross-checked against dermoscopedia, https://dermoscopedia.org/Seven_Point_Checklist. Use these instead of waiting on the Arch Dermatol paywall; the definitions are the same and the paper itself is only needed for the citation.
_sources.kawahara_2019: Kawahara J., Daneshvar S., Argenziano G., Hamarneh G., Seven-point checklist and skin lesion classification using multitask multimodal neural nets. IEEE JBHI 23(2), 2019. Derm7pt dataset and label taxonomy.
_sources.monet_2024: Kim C. et al., Transparent medical image AI via an image-text foundation model grounded in medical literature. Nature Medicine, 2024. Dermatology VLM; also the closest prior work to your H1 -- read the concept-annotation validation section before Tuesday.

_design_rationale: TIER STRUCTURE. Three wording tiers per concept, each with a matched negative.
A = short label (your existing arm).
B = Kawahara 2019 taxonomy wording -- the term as the dataset spells it.
C = Argenziano criterion definition, restated in plain visual language with the
dermatological noun removed.
WHY C IS THE ONE THAT TESTS THE HYPOTHESIS. B mostly swaps one specialist noun for
another. If CLIP never saw the vocabulary, B fails for exactly the reason A failed and
you learn nothing. C removes the term and describes only the morphology, in words that
plausibly occur in web captions. If C rescues a concept and B does not, the finding is
'CLIP has the percept but not the term' -- sharper than either 'CLIP can't see this' or
'CLIP needs the right words', and the version worth writing up.
NEGATIVES ARE THE BENIGN COUNTERPART, NOT NEGATION. CLIP handles negation poorly, so
'no blue-whitish veil' is close to useless as a contrast. The checklist itself supplies
the right negatives: it scores atypical network against typical network, and irregular
vessels against comma-shaped vessels seen in dermal nevi. Contrasting against the benign
counterpart also matches what the clinician is actually discriminating, which is the
thing you claim to be auditing.
WHAT CHANGED FROM MY FIRST DRAFT, AND WHY. Two of my tier-C descriptions were wrong
against the source definition:
pigmentation -- I emphasised asymmetric darkness. The defining feature in Argenziano's
definition is an ABRUPT CUTOFF at the edge of the pigmented area, not the asymmetry.
Corrected below. This matters because pigmentation is your one concept where a
supervised CNN reaches ~0.79 and CLIP sits at ~0.55, so it is the concept most likely
to be a wording failure rather than a hard-percept failure.
vascular structures -- the definition requires the vessels to lie OUTSIDE regression
areas, which is a spatial qualifier no single prompt can express. Noted as a known
limitation rather than papered over.
SCORING. Use score = cos(image, pos) - cos(image, neg), then AUROC against the binarised
expert grade. The difference form cancels the per-image embedding-norm effect that
inflates single-prompt AUROC. If your existing tier-A arm used cos(image, pos) alone,
rerun A in difference form or the tiers are not comparable and the grid is uninterpretable.
NULL. Score all tiers against the SAME 200-pair random-text null you already built.
Building a fresh null per tier changes the multiple-comparison accounting mid-experiment.
With 3 tiers x 4 templates x 7 concepts you are at 84 tests; carry that into Bonferroni,
not the 42 from the earlier grid.
IF YOU RUN MONET. MONET does not score concepts by raw cosine similarity -- it normalises
against a reference image set. Applying your CLIP scoring code to MONET embeddings
unchanged handicaps MONET and the comparison stops being fair. Follow their protocol or
state plainly that you used a common scoring rule for comparability and that this is a
deviation from the MONET paper.
templates: a dermoscopy photograph of a skin lesion showing {}

pigment_network.definition_source: argenziano_1998: a prominent -- hyperpigmented or broadened -- and irregular network. Histological correlate: rete ridges that are hyperpigmented or broadened, with irregular shape or distribution.

C.pos: a brown mesh whose lines are thickened and unevenly spread, with holes of differing size
C.neg: a brown mesh of thin, evenly spaced lines with holes of uniform size

pigment_network.note: Derm7pt grades this three ways (absent / typical / atypical). The A-vs-B contrast is nearly a paraphrase, so treat B as a control on wording sensitivity rather than a real intervention.

blue_whitish_veil.definition_source: argenziano_1998 (listed as gray-blue areas): irregular, confluent gray-blue to whitish-blue diffuse pigmentation, explicitly not red-blue lacunes and not maple-leaf pigmentation. Histological correlate: pigmented melanophages or melanocytes in the mid-reticular dermis.

C.pos: a merged gray-blue to milky-white haze spread over part of the surface
C.neg: clear brown and tan surface with no gray-blue haze

blue_whitish_veil.note: Your strongest concept at 0.709. Expect the smallest tier effect here -- the everyday-language and clinical descriptions nearly coincide, which is itself the explanation for why it works.

vascular_structures.definition_source: argenziano_1998 (atypical vascular pattern): linear, dotted or globular red structures, irregularly distributed, located outside areas of regression. The benign counterpart named in the source is comma-shaped vessels, typical of compound and dermal nevi.

B.pos: an atypical vascular pattern with dotted and linear irregular vessels
B.neg: regular comma-shaped vessels typical of a dermal nevus

C.pos: red dots and short red lines scattered unevenly across the surface
C.neg: a few smoothly curved red lines, evenly placed

vascular_structures.note: Known limitation: the definition's 'outside areas of regression' qualifier is not expressible in a single prompt. Kawahara et al.'s supervised CNN also struggles here and tends to predict absent, so a failure is expected and should be reported as expected, not as evidence about CLIP.

pigmentation.definition_source: argenziano_1998 (irregular diffuse pigmentation / blotches): brown, gray and black areas of diffuse pigmentation, irregular in shape or distribution, ending abruptly. Histological correlate: hyperpigmentation through all epidermal levels or upper dermis.

C.pos: a dark brown-black patch that stops abruptly instead of fading out
C.neg: brown colour that fades gradually toward the edge

pigmentation.note: The concept to watch. Supervised CNN ~0.79 vs your zero-shot ~0.55 says the signal is present in the image and CLIP is missing it -- a wording failure is the leading hypothesis, and 'abrupt cutoff' is the discriminating cue the short label never mentions. If tier C moves this one, that single row carries the paper's argument.

streaks.definition_source: argenziano_1998 (radial streaming / streaks): linear or bulbous extensions at the lesion edge, arranged radially and asymmetrically. Histological correlate: confluent radial junctional nests of melanocytes.

B.pos: irregular streaks with radial streaming and pseudopods
B.neg: regular streaks arranged symmetrically around the border

C.pos: dark finger-like projections extending outward from only part of the edge
C.neg: dark projections spaced evenly all the way around the edge

streaks.note: Already real at 0.637. 'Radiating lines' is common visual English, consistent with your reading that CLIP handles concepts describable without specialist vocabulary.

dots_and_globules.definition_source: argenziano_1998: black, brown or blue round structures, irregularly distributed within the lesion. Histological correlate: pigment aggregates in the stratum corneum, at the junction, or in the dermis.

B.pos: irregular dots and globules of varying size and distribution
B.neg: regular dots and globules of uniform size, evenly distributed

C.pos: round brown and black specks of clearly different sizes, bunched unevenly
C.neg: round brown specks of similar size, spread evenly throughout

dots_and_globules.note: Borderline at 0.613, beaten by 4/200 null pairs. Whichever way tier C moves it, report the null-beat count alongside, not just the AUROC.

regression_structures.definition_source: argenziano_1998 (regression pattern): white scar-like depigmentation and/or peppering -- multiple speckled blue-gray dots inside a hypopigmented area -- irregularly distributed. Histological correlate: pigment loss with fibroplasia and scattered dermal melanophages.

B.pos: regression structures with scar-like depigmentation and peppering
B.neg: a lesion without regression or depigmented areas

C.pos: a white scar-like area sprinkled with fine blue-gray dots
C.neg: even pigmentation with no white scar-like patch

regression_structures.note: Borderline at 0.649. The definition is genuinely two visual things (white area, peppering) fused into one label -- if tier C fails, worth reporting the two halves as separate prompts as a small ablation, since that failure mode is about label composition rather than vocabulary.
